"OUR LIFE", NOVEMBER 7, 1941
( Jewish weekly newspaper, 30 R-te Cardinal Mercier )
Editor - Mr. D.S.Rabinovich

THE ASHKENAZI JEWISH COMMUNAL ASSOCIATION IN SHANGHAI

NOTICE

The Committee of the Ashkenazi Jewish Communal Association in Shanghai, having considered at its meeting of 3-11-41 the budget of the Association for 1941/42 and also the resolution of the Russian Emigrants Committee, in accordance with which Russian emigrants of Jewish origin will, as from 1-11-41, make payments of their voluntary income tax direct to the Russian Emigrants Committee and not through the medium of the Association, decided:-

(1) that members of the Association be requested to pay to the Association all voluntary income tax in arrears up to November 1, 1941, after which the money collected will be distributed in accordance with the previously made arrangements;

(2) that members of the Association who are Russian emigrants be informed that payment of the voluntary income tax to the Russian Emigrants Committee direct does not exempt them from the payment of 50% of the previously approved self-taxation for the needs of the Association;

(3) that voluntary self-taxation approved by the Association in respect of members other than Russian emigrants, remains in force.

Committee of the Shanghai Jewish Ashkenazi Communal Association.

10-11-41.

上海阿什肯纳兹犹太公会协会

通告

上海阿什肯纳兹犹太公会协会委员会在1941年11月3日的会议上审议了协会1941/42年度预算，以及俄国流亡者委员会的一项决议。根据该决议，具有犹太血统的俄国流亡者自1941年11月1日起，将其自愿所得税直接支付给俄国流亡者委员会，而非通过本协会转交。据此决定：-

(1) 请协会会员向本协会缴清截至1941年11月1日的所有拖欠自愿所得税，此后所收款项将按此前作出的安排进行分配；

(2) 告知身为俄国流亡者的协会会员，直接向俄国流亡者委员会缴纳自愿所得税，并不免除其缴纳先前批准的、用于协会需求的自征税额的50%；

(3) 协会批准的针对非俄国流亡者会员的自愿自征税规定继续有效。

上海犹太阿什肯纳兹公会协会委员会。

SUBJECT: Central European Refugees - To Leave Japan for Shanghai - Press Reports
（批：Lo 5/26144 D.I.）

With reference to the attached
press reports which indicate that between 800
and 1000 Jewish refugees are likely to arrive
in Shanghai in the near future from Japan, no
information is available locally as to the
correctness of such details. It is possible,
however, that a large number of Polish Jews
will arrive shortly from Kobe en route to Australia,
New Zealand and Palestine. No immigration
permits have been issued by this office in
respect of these persons.

149 Polish Jewish refugees arrived
in Shanghai ex Kobe in the ss. Kamakura Maru
on August 4. The Majority of them have already
left these shores en route to Australasia and
Palestine.

TAIRIKU SHIMPO :-

800 JEWISH REFUGEES IN KOBE TO BE SENT TO
SHANGHAI OWING TO FREEZING ORDER

The Jewish Association in Kobe was
receiving Yen 130,000 per month for about 800 Jewish
refugees in Kobe from the "American Joint Relief Fund
For Jewish Refugees" in New York. The money was remitted
through the Kobe Branch of the New York National City
Bank and divided among the refugees so as to enable them
to maintain their livelihood, each refugee receiving
about Yen 1.05 a day.
Owing to the Freezing Order, the
remittance from America has ceased and it has been decided
that the 800 Jews be sent to Shanghai or to Australia.
More than 300 Jewish emigrants are expected in Shanghai
from Kobe on August 20 and a similar number on August 30.

SUBJECT: POLISH JEWISH REFUGEES - Letter dated
July 5, 1941 from H. B. M. Consulate-
General addressed to the Secretary &
Commissioner General, S.M.C.

（批：Cl, 5/22/44 / BI.）

The contents of the second paragraph of the
attached communication are interesting to this
office in that the points raised are in accord, in
the main, with the views voiced by us in a report
dated March 19, 1941 on the same subject. Since
March 24, 1941 when the Shanghai Municipal Council
granted permission to Messrs. Szczupakiewicz and
Warhaftig to apply for the immigration into Shanghai
of some 300 Polish citizens (refugees) who desired
eventually to proceed to Palestine, 146 Immigration
Certificates have been issued. 51 persons of
this number arrived in Shanghai on May 1, 1941 from
Vladivostock in the ss. Adtika, a Soviet steamer, but
none has proceeded to Palestine from Shanghai as far
as is known. Four, however, have left these parts
for the United States.

While it is learned that there are still a
certain number of refugees, of various nationalities,
in Vladivostock, doubt is expressed as to how
they can proceed to Shanghai since no direct trans-
portation facilities now exist between the two ports.

In view of the incidence of hostilities between
the Soviet Union and Germany, the Siberian route to
the Far East from Europe via Dairen has been closed
and the probability of refugees arriving in Shanghai
from Central Europe by the Siberia-Dairen-Shanghai
route can now be considered extremely remote.

URGENT
（批：d.b.(CYSB)）
Commr. of Police.

附件通信第二段的内容引起本处关注，因为其中提出的观点与我们在1941年3月19日关于同一主题的报告中所表达的观点基本一致。自1941年3月24日上海公共租界工部局批准Szczupakiewicz先生和Warhaftig先生申请约300名希望最终前往巴勒斯坦的波兰公民（难民）入境上海以来，已签发了146份入境证书。这批人中有51人于1941年5月1日乘坐苏联轮船“阿迪卡”号（ss. Adtika）从符拉迪沃斯托克抵达上海，但据所知，无人从上海前往巴勒斯坦。不过，有四人已离开本地区前往美国。

虽然获悉符拉迪沃斯托克仍有若干不同国籍的难民，但对于他们如何能前往上海表示怀疑，因为目前两港之间不存在直接的交通工具。

鉴于苏联与德国之间爆发敌对行动，经大连从欧洲通往远东的西伯利亚路线已关闭，因此现在可以认为，难民经由西伯利亚-大连-上海路线从中欧抵达上海的可能性极小。

July 5th, 1941.

My dear Phillips,

You will of course recall the various conversations and discussions which took place earlier on in the year between ourselves, the Polish Legation, and the two Polish Jew representatives (Messrs. Szczupakiewicz and Warhaftig), in connection with the entry into Shanghai of 300 Polish Jew refugees then in Kovno, the main details of which were embodied in the Consul-General's official letter to you of March 22nd.

I have not since heard from either the two delegates or the Polish Legation as to whether these refugees eventually proceeded further or what happened to them. Political events move so rapidly these days, however, that they may in the end have been unable to leave Soviet territory or may even have preferred to stay where they were, rather than proceed to Palestine under present conditions. On the other side of the picture, of course, the position has altered materially in consequence of recent developments in the Near and Middle East, and we have just received official advice not only that the difficulty of passage in transit through India and Egypt is increasing, but also that the Government of Palestine have withheld approval of the immigration quota for the quarter ended June 30th and are at present unable to indicate the prospects of allotting a quota subsequently. In other words the prospects of these, and still less any other, refugees from Soviet territory, or elsewhere, being able to obtain admission into Palestine in the near future must now be regarded as too problematical to be taken into serious account in considering any further applications for temporary residence in the Settlement which may be received on behalf of such persons. The Immigration and Travel Section of the Government of Palestine have suggested that the Council might be apprised of these developments against the eventuality of similar requests for entry facilities en route to Palestine being addressed to them in future.

I might appropriately mention in this connection that I received a visit on June 11th from a Mr. Issai G. Rosovsky, described on his card as "President of Hias of America, Japan Branch, Kobe", a Litmanian, who solicited the good offices of this Consulate-General with a view to obtaining an official statement that a number of Litmanian Jewish refugees, then

亲爱的菲利普斯：

你当然会记得今年早些时候我们之间、波兰公使馆以及两位波兰犹太代表（Szczupakiewicz先生和Warhaftig先生）就当时在考纳斯的300名波兰犹太难民进入上海一事进行的各种谈话和讨论，其主要细节已体现在总领事3月22日给你的正式信函中。

此后，我未从这两位代表或波兰公使馆处得知这些难民是否最终继续前行或其下落如何。然而，如今的政治局势变化迅速，他们最终可能无法离开苏联领土，或者甚至可能倾向于留在原地，而不是在目前条件下前往巴勒斯坦。另一方面，由于近东和中东最近的局势发展，情况已发生重大变化，我们刚刚收到官方通知，不仅经由印度和埃及的过境通行难度日益增加，而且巴勒斯坦政府已扣留截至6月30日的季度移民配额批准，目前也无法指示后续分配配额的前景。换言之，在考虑今后可能收到的代表此类人员申请在租界临时居留的任何进一步申请时，必须认为这些难民，更不用说来自苏联领土或其他地方的任何其他难民，在不久的将来能够获得巴勒斯坦入境许可的前景过于不确定，不足以予以认真考虑。巴勒斯坦政府移民和旅行部门建议，工部局应知悉这些动态，以备将来有类似的途经巴勒斯坦入境设施的请求向他们提出时有所准备。

在此适当提及，我于6月11日接待了一位名为Issai G. Rosovsky先生的来访，他的名片上注明其为“美国希阿斯组织（Hias of America）日本分部、神户主席”，立陶宛人，他请求本总领事馆施以援手，以期获得一份官方声明，证明当时一批立陶宛犹太难民，然后

With reference to the contents of the
attached letter, it seems perfectly manifest that
the Japanese authorities in Kobe desire to evict
the 1600 refugees now staying at that port into
points where they will not have the "nuisance value"
that they apparently do at present. Shanghai is
the logical place to send them since the restrictions
here in regard to immigration are by no means as
stringent as they should be. In the past the
Shanghai Municipal Council has enforced the current
immigration regulations only in close co-operation
with the various travel and shipping companies.

----------------------------------------------------------------

In accordance with instructions
received, the Consul-General for Poland, Mr.
de Rosset (who has been away in Japan on business
for a considerable period), was interviewed by
D.S.I. Pitts on September 9, in regard to details
relating to the proposed immigration into Shanghai
of Polish refugees.

Matters of registration, the
issue of permits, depositing of funds to ensure
that immigrants did not become a public burden,
etc., etc., were touched upon and the Counsul-
General promised his full co-operation in all
details. As, however, there is at present no
indication of the arrival of Polish refugees in
Shanghai, the Consul-General asked that the matter
be left in abeyance. He will seek the assistance
of this office as soon as he receives information
that Polish refugees desire to take up residence
in Shanghai.
